# Actual smooth deepest-source example with an inside transition surviving the normal PSD budget

This exact example tests the new cap-normal Hessian constraint. It retains an actual convex lattice-complete body, the tied H buffer, all ambient cap orientations, a unique global deepest source, and an actual minimizing cap with both inside and outside half-selected limiting facets. Its limiting PSD transition budget is equality. Thus that constraint cannot by itself eliminate inside selectors. The body is not a bad-body minimum and the example does not refute OC or a possible global Gamma_d/k payment.

## 1. The body and its exact normalization

Use n=d=1. Set sigma=sqrt(5/24). Choose epsilon,h>0 small, put

    H=h sigma, Y=sigma(epsilon+h)/2,

and assume Y+H<1/2. Define three fibers

    K_-1=[-1,0], K_0=[Y-1,Y+1], K_1=[0,1],

and let C be their convex hull at bases -1,0,1. Its projection is [-1,1], so these are all sampled bases. The average endpoint interval [-1/2,1/2] lies in K_0 because Y<1/2; hence convex-hull interpolation adds nothing to the prescribed middle fiber. Thus C is a full-dimensional convex body with exactly these positive sampled fibers.

The total mixed mass is M=4. Its pooled WITHIN-fiber covariance is independent of the middle translation:

    Sigma=(1^3+2^3+1^3)/(12M)=5/24=sigma^2.

For an interval [c-L/2,c+L/2], direct minimization of the d=1 projective energy gives

    E(c+t)=L[1-(2t/L)^2].

Consequently its tied profile is

    f_H(c+t)=(L/M)sqrt(1-(2t/L)^2),

and at the middle center f_H(Y)=1/2. In particular the displayed Y is exactly the sum of the physical source buffer epsilon sigma/2 and half the physical smoothing width H/2. There is no normalization chosen independently of the actual H profile.

## 2. Own depths and the unique global source

In an interval, choose the cap pointing toward the closer endpoint. Its uniform outward smoothed capture is at most

    L/2-|t|+epsilon sigma f_H(c+t)+H/2.

This follows by averaging ordinary outward tail lengths, each bounded above by its untruncated linear length. Since f_H is uniquely maximal at t=0, the own smooth depth is uniquely maximal at c, with value

    L/2+epsilon sigma L/M+H/2

when the parameters are small enough that the centered transition interval is proper. For the middle fiber this value is 1+Y.

At any middle mark x, a sufficiently large finite base tilt captures exactly one complete outer interval, misses the other, and leaves its chosen own cap unchanged. Thus its mixed depth is at most 1 plus its own depth, with strict upper bound 2+Y unless x=Y. At an outer base, an exposing tilt isolates its own cap, so its mixed depth is at most 1/2+epsilon sigma/4+H/2, strictly less than 2+Y.

It remains to check EVERY ambient cap at (0,Y). A nonvertical normal has one of the two continuous orientations. Normalize the physical continuous coefficient to +1 or -1, and write A for its arbitrary physical base coefficient.

For orientation +1, the actual through-source cap integrand is

    Psi((x+A z-H/2)/H).

Pair x in K_1=[0,1] with -x in K_-1=[-1,0]. Their kernel arguments sum to -1, so CDF symmetry makes their kernel values sum EXACTLY to one. The entire outer capture is therefore exactly 1, for EVERY A. The middle capture equals 1+Y. Thus every such positive-orientation cap has mass exactly 2+Y.

For orientation -1, the integrand is

    Psi((-x+A z+Y+epsilon sigma/2)/H).

The paired outer arguments have nonnegative sum, hence their CDF values sum to at least one. The middle capture is again 1+Y. So every negative-orientation cap has mass at least 2+Y, and a finite sufficiently large tilt attains equality by saturating one outer fiber and emptying the other.

Closed pure-base caps through zero contain the whole middle fiber and at least one outer fiber, so their mass is at least 3>2+Y. The zero continuous normal has therefore also been checked.

It follows that (0,Y) is the UNIQUE actual global deepest point and

    Q=2+Y, beta=(2+Y)/4.

This is an all-ambient proof, not a test of a prescribed finite menu alone. A balanced actual two-cap menu consists of the untilted positive-orientation cap and one large-tilt negative-orientation cap; their continuous balance weights are 1/2 because grad_x f_H(Y)=0.

## 3. Exact transition selectors and the PSD equality

Consider the untilted positive-orientation cap. Its physical threshold is H/2. At x=0 on both outer endpoint facets its kernel argument is -1/2, so W=1/2.

At base -1 the cap is asymptotically OUTSIDE-supporting at the interval's top endpoint. Its section selector is tau_out=W=1/2. At base +1 it is asymptotically INSIDE-supporting at the interval's bottom endpoint, with tau_in=1-W=1/2. These allocations arise from this single actual family of convex bodies, so all common-roof compatibility requirements are retained.

The positive-width section masses at the two outer bases are both sigma/2; the middle section mass is sigma. Thus the exact kernel base centroid is zero. The source is proper in its own fiber, as required by the smoothing construction.

The two physical endpoint planes are x=-H/2 and x=+H/2. At the lower plane, the outside fiber -1 and the middle fiber contribute their full section coareas; at the upper plane, the inside fiber +1 and the middle fiber contribute. No endpoint trace ambiguity occurs. After normalization the common coarea is sigma. Both outer transition densities chi equal ONE, although their section selectors tau equal one half.

For d=1 the normalized continuous normal has no nontrivial transverse direction. A base variation k=a' z therefore gives

    outside transition quadratic mass = (a')^2
                                        = inside transition quadratic mass.

The proper middle contributions cancel, the base-block correction is zero, and the complete normal Hessian constraint is equality. In fact the positive-orientation cap mass is constant in A, as already proved, so its base-normal Hessian vanishes exactly at every width.

One can choose h=o(epsilon) while keeping all formulas exact. As both parameters tend to zero, the limiting source is (0,0), the same two supporting allocations remain one half, and the transition covariance comparison stays equality.

## 4. Exact scope

This is not in the below-sharp regime: beta tends to 1/2, whereas the OC target for n=d=1 is 1/4. No actual body-stress separator at a global body minimum is asserted. The example proves the narrower and relevant point that coherent convex-body provenance, global source deepestness, the exact first kernel moment, and the new full normal PSD condition do NOT force inside-support section selectors to vanish. A successful use of the Hessian must extract a quantitative global cost, or combine it with the bad-body/minor-mass information, rather than claim such an elimination.
